pass_a_gloss: What need is there for my silence, which many others have often, but I especially now, being willing and unwilling, being forced to be silent and to keep silent. For I have neglected and I am ignorant of these good and fine words, which are spoken or composed by the chosen and approved names and verbs in a certain uninterrupted sequence. But I, being less capable of this pleasant Greek work, have not been able to accomplish it. But now, for eight years, I have not even spoken or written anything great or small, nor have I heard anyone else speaking or writing, except for these wonderful men who have established the beautiful philosophy, who care little for flattery and the smoothness of names. They, placing their voices second, wish to examine and proclaim the matters themselves with precision. I do not think they do not wish to, but rather they very much wish to, and they pour out the good and precise thoughts with ease and clarity in speech. But perhaps they are not able to do so, having the sacred and divine word in their minds, and the pleasant word in their speech, to encompass the soul of each individual, which is very difficult. For if silence is somehow a friend and helper to the mind and discovery, the eloquent man is not found anywhere else, but in voices and the continuous practice of them. And the mind learns something else, and the mouth is bound by the tongue, if I wanted to say something, even small, to the voice of the Greeks, our wonderful leaders, who now direct the affairs of all men under the human rule, not being ignorant or unlearned, being precise and varied and wonderful, and being called completely Greek, having been expressed and handed down in the Roman language, which is persuasive and boastful and conforming to the royal authority, but burdensome to me. But in no other way is it possible or desirable for me, since our words are like certain images of the passions of our soul, and to those who are able to speak, like good painters and skilled craftsmen, who write with colors and matter, not only similar, but also varied and very beautiful, with a mixture of flowers, we would agree that they are able to write without any hindrance.

pass_b_english: What need is there for my silence, which many others have often maintained, but I especially now, being willing and unwilling, being forced to be silent and to keep silent? For I have neglected and I am ignorant of these good and fine words, which are spoken or composed by the chosen and approved names and verbs in a certain uninterrupted sequence. But I, being less capable of this pleasant Greek work, have not been able to accomplish it. Now, for eight years, I have not even spoken or written anything great or small, nor have I heard anyone else speaking or writing, except for these wonderful men who have established the beautiful philosophy, who care little for flattery and the smoothness of names. They place their voices second and wish to examine and proclaim the matters themselves with precision, pouring out the good and precise thoughts with ease and clarity in speech. Perhaps they are not able to do so, having the sacred and divine word in their minds, and the pleasant word in their speech, to encompass the soul of each individual, which is very difficult. If silence is somehow a friend and helper to the mind and discovery, the eloquent man is not found anywhere else, but in voices and the continuous practice of them. The mind learns something else, and the mouth is bound by the tongue, if I wanted to say something, even small, to the voice of the Greeks, our wonderful leaders, who now direct the affairs of all men under the human rule, being precise and varied and wonderful, and being called completely Greek, having been expressed and handed down in the Roman language, which is persuasive and boastful and conforming to the royal authority, but burdensome to me. In no other way is it possible or desirable for me, since our words are like certain images of the passions of our soul, and to those who are able to speak, like good painters and skilled craftsmen, who write with colors and matter, not only similar, but also varied and very beautiful, with a mixture of flowers, we would agree that they are able to write without any hindrance. The Lord has given them this gift, and they use it to proclaim the truth, so that all may hear and understand, and I am grateful for their eloquence, which is a gift from God.
